verdicts.evidence: Without `.sort()` the manifest read order, hence the order of `derivation.notes`, follows the filesystem. Measured with `fs.readdirSync` patched to return reverse order before the ESM binding: baseline notes stay `[aaa read, mmm read, zzz unread]`, the mutant emits `[zzz unread, mmm read, aaa read]`. The machine emission stops being comparable from one filesystem to another.

verdicts.evidence: When `contested` is empty the guarded block is a no-op: `filter(b => !contested.includes(b.path))` is the identity and the `for (const p of contested)` body never runs. Measured: with `if (true)` the deriveAll/deriveCloudflareWorkers JSON is byte-identical over 12 hand-built wrangler projects, 4 real `rules --for --json` runs (contested mission, multi-entry mission, unreadable root, the runward repo) and 123 randomly generated projects (4591 bindings).

verdicts.evidence: The Set is filled by iterating `all.bindings`, which are pushed file by file in `found` order, and `found` is already `.sort()`ed, so the spread is monotone and `.sort()` is a no-op. Measured: the ambiguous note's `file` field is byte-identical on contested fixtures with 2, 3 and 6 manifests, both with the native readdir and with an `fs.readdirSync` patched (via `node -r`, before the ESM binding) to return reverse order.
